lessons.title: Africa and the world
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level III — Social Studies (geography, history, citizenship); to be checked against the official texts
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Name the seven continents and the five oceans.
Describe Africa: its regions, big rivers, mountains and lakes.
Name organisations that Cameroon belongs to.
reviewNotes: Facts about Cameroon are limited to well-established, neutral points; dates and names to be checked by a teacher against the official textbook.

Number of African countries (54) is the number of UN-recognised states and some books give a different number; 'longest river' and 'highest mountain' are standard textbook facts. CEMAC membership and the FCFA are well known; some details of membership are simplified.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Continents and oceans
blocks.md: There are **seven continents**: Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania (Australia) and Antarctica. There are **five oceans**: the Pacific (the biggest), the Atlantic, the Indian, the Southern and the Arctic. Cameroon is in **Africa**, on the Atlantic coast.

blocks.caption: The seven continents.
blocks.alt: Seven boxes with the continents Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania and Antarctica, each with one example.

blocks.title: Africa
blocks.md: Africa is the **second biggest continent**. The **Equator** crosses it. It has about **54 countries** and five regions: North, West, Central, East and Southern Africa. Cameroon is in **Central Africa**. Famous features: the **Sahara** (the biggest hot desert), the **River Nile** (the longest river in Africa), the **Congo River**, **Mount Kilimanjaro** (the highest mountain in Africa) and **Lake Victoria** (the biggest lake in Africa).

blocks.title: Cameroon and other countries
blocks.md: Cameroon belongs to the **United Nations**, the **African Union**, the **Commonwealth** and the **Francophonie** (it is a member of both because it has English and French). It is a member of **CEMAC**, a group of six Central African countries that share the FCFA currency: Cameroon, Chad, the Central African Republic, the Republic of the Congo, Gabon and Equatorial Guinea. These groups help countries to trade, keep peace and share ideas.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Calling Africa a country: it is a **continent** with many countries.
- Saying that Cameroon is in North Africa or East Africa.
- Mixing continents and oceans.
- Saying that all Africans speak the same language: Africa has hundreds of languages.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Name the ocean next to Cameroon and the continent where Cameroon is.
steps: Cameroon has a coast on the Atlantic Ocean.
It is in the continent of Africa, in Central Africa.
blocks.answer: The Atlantic Ocean; the continent of Africa (Central Africa).

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Name one great river, one mountain and one desert in Africa.
blocks.answer: The Nile, Mount Kilimanjaro and the Sahara.

lessons.title: Map skills: direction, symbols, scale and grid references
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level III — Social Studies (geography, history, citizenship); to be checked against the official texts
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Use the eight points of the compass.
Read a map key (symbols) and a simple scale.
Give and read a grid reference.
reviewNotes: Facts about Cameroon are limited to well-established, neutral points; dates and names to be checked by a teacher against the official textbook.
Mnemonic 'Never Eat Soggy Waffles' is a common memory aid, not a fact; the teacher may replace it. A blue line = river is the usual convention; check the map key each time.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Compass directions
blocks.md: The four main directions are **North, East, South and West**. Between them are North-East (NE), South-East (SE), South-West (SW) and North-West (NW). On most maps **North is at the top**. A **compass** shows the direction: its needle points to the north. To remember the order, say: **N**ever **E**at **S**oggy **W**affles (clockwise).

blocks.caption: The eight points of the compass.
blocks.alt: A compass rose with eight arms. The labels are N at the top, E at the right, S at the bottom, W at the left, and NE, SE, SW, NW between them.

blocks.title: Map key and scale
blocks.md: A **map key** (legend) explains the **symbols** on a map: a blue line for a river, a black line for a road, a dot for a town. The **scale** tells how real distances are shown on the map. If the scale is **1 cm to 20 km**, then 1 cm on the map is 20 km on the ground. To find the real distance: **measure on the map, then multiply** by the scale.

blocks.title: Grid references
blocks.md: A grid map is divided into squares. The columns have **letters** (A, B, C, D) and the rows have **numbers** (1, 2, 3, 4). To give a **grid reference**, say the **letter first and then the number**: B2. A **physical map** shows relief and water; a **political map** shows countries, regions and towns; latitudes run east-west and longitudes north-south.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Forgetting that north is at the **top** of a map.
- Multiplying by the wrong number, or forgetting to use the scale.
- Giving the number before the letter in a grid reference.
- Measuring a distance from the edge of the ruler instead of from the 0 mark.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: On a map with a scale of 1 cm to 20 km, two towns are 4.5 cm apart. What is the real distance?

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: In the grid picture, in which square is the school?
steps: The school is in the second column (B) and the second row.
